# ServiceNow Security Center
## Secure instance configuration

### Customer responsibility
Users can monitor the [ServiceNow Security Center (SSC)](https://www.servicenow.com) to review hardening settings, security scanner outcomes, and metrics related to instance security. Customers are required to prioritize hardening configuration options in Security Center according to their organization’s requirements.

---

### Best practices

#### Establish security hardening priorities
Collaborate with relevant stakeholders to develop a comprehensive hardening plan related to a ServiceNow instance that aligns with the organization’s security strategy and priorities. Create a process to apply the plan to a ServiceNow instance using the security hardening setting in ServiceNow Security Center.

---

## Best practices

### Choose an encryption method for data at rest in an instance*
The customer’s security team should work with stakeholders to thoroughly assess the regulatory and organizational requirements for data stored in their ServiceNow instance(s) to determine if data at rest needs to be encrypted.

Based on this assessment, customers should select the most appropriate encryption method offered by ServiceNow. When implementing the chosen encryption method, ensure encryption settings and key management are configured in accordance with internal policies and compliance standards to safeguard sensitive information throughout its lifecycle.

### Customers seeking included functionality
**Field Encryption Starter**:  
Data stored within a ServiceNow instance can be protected with Field Encryption Starter, which allows customers to encrypt specific fields within the instance using AES128 or AES256 encryption.

---

## Best practices

### Configure mobile application security controls
Collaborate with stakeholders to determine the configuration of built-in mobile security controls. The [Data Processing Addendum (DPA)](https://www.servicenow.com) reflects the customer's agreement regarding personal data. The DPA also defines the roles of the **data controller** and **data processor**, and describes the nature, scope, and purpose of the processing.

sentences:
## Evaluate and configure AI model options on the ServiceNow AI Platform
Some ServiceNow products rely on third-party Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEM) services, such as Azure OpenAI. Collaborate with your stakeholders to determine whether your organization will use these cloud-based models. If they do not meet your security or compliance requirements, configure ServiceNow to fully opt out of options like Microsoft Azure OpenAI, Google Gemini, or Anthropic Claude on Amazon Web Services (AWS).

*Note:* Certain skills may restrict model provider selection, based on functional or technical limitations. These exceptions are described in [Model Provider Support Matrix for Now Assist Skills and AI Agents (KB2222333)](https://www.servicenow.com/kb/article?sys_kb_id=kb2222333), which outlines supported skills and agents for both the Now LLM and third-party OEM LLMs.

```markdown
# PROTECT  
## Vulnerability management  

### Customer responsibility  
Customers should apply patches and upgrades in a timely manner and test all configuration changes in a non-production instance before deploying to production. To maintain support and security, customers must ensure their instances comply with ServiceNow EOL.

### ServiceNow responsibility  
ServiceNow maintains an ongoing infrastructure vulnerability program described in the [Commercial Cloud vulnerability management SOP](#), using third-party commercial and in-house tools to identify vulnerabilities in the ServiceNow perimeter and for all cloud and corporate systems ([link](#) requires access to the ServiceNow CORE Compliance Portal, find out how to access core [here](#)). There are two releases of the ServiceNow AI Platform per year. In addition, patches and hotfixes are produced throughout the supported lifetime of a major release and rolled into the codebase for inclusion in the next version.

## Data processing in production
When using generative AI services, prompts and responses are processed in memory only—inputs and outputs are not stored or cached by the inference infrastructure. For details on how data is transmitted, processed, and protected during runtime, refer to the [Data Processing for Advanced AI & Data Products FAQ (KB1584492)](https://www.servicenow.com/kb/article?sys_kb_id=kb1584492).

Evaluate how AI data is securely processed and select either ServiceNow-hosted or third-party LLMs in alignment with your organization’s data residency and governance policies.

*Note:* Third-party LLMs may use global infrastructure to dynamically route traffic to the best available data center for each request. This means the regional processing location may differ from the data center region specified on a customer’s order form.

## Understand the difference between Allow-If and Deny-Unless ACLs
Allow-If allows access upon successful evaluation and is the default ACL. Deny-Unless denies access unless there is a successful evaluation. Deny-Unless ACLs will take priority against Allow-If ACLs in ACL Evaluation as it will be evaluated first. The Deny-Unless ACL defines the users that will NOT be denied. Said another way, the user will be denied access unless the role, condition, and script requirements are met.

## Verify Security Jump Start—ACL Rules Plugin is enabled
All new ServiceNow instances have the [Security Jump Start—ACL Rules plugin](#) installed to provide a base level of access security for key system tables. Use this plugin to establish foundational ACL protections for sensitive system data.

## Evaluate and configure AI model options on the ServiceNow AI Platform
Some ServiceNow products rely on third-party Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEM) services, such as Azure OpenAI. Collaborate with your stakeholders to determine whether your organization will use these cloud-based models. If they do not meet your security or compliance requirements, configure ServiceNow to fully opt out of options like Microsoft Azure OpenAI, Google Gemini, or Anthropic Claude on Amazon Web Services (AWS).

*Note:* Certain skills may restrict model provider selection, based on functional or technical limitations. These exceptions are described in [Model Provider Support Matrix for Now Assist Skills and AI Agents (KB2222333)](https://www.servicenow.com/kb/article?sys_kb_id=kb2222333), which outlines supported skills and agents for both the Now LLM and third-party OEM LLMs.

```markdown
# The Shared Responsibility Model

Security is a partnership between ServiceNow and the customer, both with specific responsibilities. Therefore, it is essential that each party understands their role in this partnership. Using the extensive capabilities of the ServiceNow AI Platform, customers can configure instances to meet their unique security policies and obligations while also complying with any regional or industry-specific requirements.

- **As the data controller**, the customer determines access rights to their instance and the data it contains. Security controls within the instance enable customers to implement policies appropriate to their own requirements and make decisions on data classification.

- **As the data processor**, ServiceNow secures the platform infrastructure and provides tools for security management and monitoring according to customer requirements.

```markdown
### Best practices continued

#### Understand Account recovery (ACR) capabilities
When utilizing Single Sign-On (SSO), ensure that at least one Account Recovery (ACR) administrator is registered prior to activation. This precaution secures fallback access to critical systems should primary authentication methods become misconfigured or unavailable. Thoroughly document all ACR procedures, limit access strictly to authorized personnel, and regularly audit ACR usage to uphold strong security standards. Restrict local logins for interactive sessions to approved recovery users with MFA enabled and employ ACR solely as a recovery tool to maintain system integrity.

Collaborate with relevant stakeholders to fully understand how anonymized data is shared with ServiceNow. Confirm the intended data contribution strategy with appropriate stakeholders. Customers of the Advanced AI and Data Products can opt out of sharing data.

Regularly review event logs for login activity and privilege escalation to identify and respond to potential security threats. Event logs provide insights into system activity, including successful and failed login attempts and privilege escalation events.

Routinely monitor system logs to detect configuration changes, system errors, and unusual data connections that may indicate security or operational issues. System logs contain information about general activity, including configuration changes, system errors, workflows, and inbound/outbound data connections.

# Cloud infrastructure security management

## ServiceNow responsibility

ServiceNow is responsible for maintaining a secure architecture within customer cloud environments. This includes implementing hardened configurations and supporting processes to protect sensitive data and ensure system integrity. Security measures in place include firewalls, secure logical access controls, and intrusion detection systems. ServiceNow also continuously monitors systems for vulnerabilities and malicious activity.

As the SaaS Cloud Solution Provider, ServiceNow manages the cloud infrastructure to ensure availability, scalability, security, and performance. Responsibilities include:

- Developing and enforcing security policies and controls
- Monitoring for potential threats
- Implementing access controls
- Ensuring compliance with applicable regulations and industry standards

It is important to understand default MFA for local logins, high-privilege accounts, and sensitive roles. Teams should ensure that this default MFA setting is communicated to all relevant stakeholders. If a ServiceNow instance is not yet upgraded, enabling MFA for all admin users is recommended.

## Customer responsibility
Customers are responsible to thoroughly review, select and configure the file transfer methods and web services settings used within the instance, ensuring that all security configurations align with their organization’s policies and standards.

### Use encryption to secure outbound file transfers during transit
Outbound file transfers from a customer’s instance should use secure protocols such as SFTP, FTPS, or SCP to protect data in transit. Outbound clear text protocols such as FTP and HTTP are also supported but not recommended. Inbound transfers such as web uploads are conducted exclusively over HTTPS.

### Consider limiting file attachment types
Collaborate with stakeholders to determine whether file attachments should be limited by file extension and MIME type. This approach can help prevent potentially malicious files from being uploaded and stored in the instance.

Outbound file transfers from a customer’s instance should use secure protocols such as SFTP, FTPS, or SCP to protect data in transit. ## Understand the difference between Allow-If and Deny-Unless ACLs
Allow-If allows access upon successful evaluation and is the default ACL. Deny-Unless denies access unless there is a successful evaluation. Deny-Unless ACLs will take priority against Allow-If ACLs in ACL Evaluation as it will be evaluated first. The Deny-Unless ACL defines the users that will NOT be denied. ## Backup restoration
If a customer deletes data inadvertently, or if a customer's data integration or automation gets misconfigured or malfunctions, this could render data unusable or inaccessible. In these scenarios, AHA architecture would not be able to recover the deleted data or data loss due to misconfiguration, because with AHA database replication occurs to both instances in the pair at near real-time. Media disposal and destruction refers to the disposal of hard drives in ServiceNow colocation facilities. ServiceNow follows NIST 800-88 guidelines for destroying hard drives and rendering the media infeasible for future use.

ServiceNow has separate business continuity plans and processes, which are tested annually, in place to ensure availability for the ServiceNow corporate organization and the services it relies on.

#### Advanced High Availability (AHA) architecture
ServiceNow colocation facilities are arranged in regional pairs, with all customer production data hosted in both colocation facilities simultaneously. ServiceNow uses asynchronous database replication to keep these pairs in sync.

When performing maintenance, or if an infrastructure component fails, transfer between active and passive colocation facilities is executed as part of ServiceNow standard operating procedures. This ensures that when AHA is needed to address an instance failure, the transfer will be successful and service disruption minimized.

The assessment typically spans several months and follows an iterative process where findings are remediated by ServiceNow security and development teams. Results of these penetration tests are available to customers and prospects under NDA via the ServiceNow CORE Compliance Portal.

### Create a process to examine ServiceNow penetration test reports periodically
Create a process to ensure stakeholders, such as your security team, review the most recent published [ServiceNow penetration test reports](#) on the ServiceNow CORE Compliance Portal. Find out how to access CORE [here](#).

#### Classify data in the instance
Data classification is available to all customers and enables the identification and classification of stored data for each instance, ensuring that data controls meet organizational requirements, as agreed by the stakeholders.

Data classification is for data that is known. Data discovery allows the discovery of data in comment fields, description fields, or attachments. Data anonymization can be used to mitigate issues and limit risk.

#### Allocate roles within the instance according to data access requirements
Identify which individuals are authorized to access data according to its classification, document these permissions, and establish roles that align with expected access requirements.

# ServiceNow responsibility continued

## Backup restoration
If a customer deletes data inadvertently, or if a customer's data integration or automation gets misconfigured or malfunctions, this could render data unusable or inaccessible. In these scenarios, AHA architecture would not be able to recover the deleted data or data loss due to misconfiguration, because with AHA database replication occurs to both instances in the pair at near real-time. Restoring from **backup** is the only option for recovery.

ServiceNow can restore customer data upon request. For more information, see the [ServiceNow Backup and Restoration SOP](#) (link requires access to the ServiceNow CORE Compliance Portal. Find out how to access CORE [here](#)).

## Media disposal and destruction
Media disposal and destruction refers to the disposal of hard drives in ServiceNow colocation facilities. ServiceNow follows NIST 800-88 guidelines for destroying hard drives and rendering the media infeasible for future use.

---

```markdown
# Best practices continued

## Know the difference between software updates and upgrades
Understanding the difference between a software update and an upgrade is essential for maintaining both security and support in your ServiceNow environment.

- **Software updates:** Patches and platform fixes delivered throughout the year via the ServiceNow Patching Program. These address known vulnerabilities and improve performance without changing the platform version.
- **Upgrades:** Moving to a newer major platform version, typically released twice a year, which includes enhanced features, architectural improvements, and broader functionality.

Both are critical but serve different purposes in keeping your instance secure, stable, and supported.

This guide is specifically designed for instance administrators to collaborate closely with security and compliance professionals. ## Data processing in production
When using generative AI services, prompts and responses are processed in memory only—inputs and outputs are not stored or cached by the inference infrastructure. For details on how data is transmitted, processed, and protected during runtime, refer to the [Data Processing for Advanced AI & Data Products FAQ (KB1584492)](https://www.servicenow.com/kb/article?sys_kb_id=kb1584492).

Evaluate how AI data is securely processed and select either ServiceNow-hosted or third-party LLMs in alignment with your organization’s data residency and governance policies.

*Note:* Third-party LLMs may use global infrastructure to dynamically route traffic to the best available data center for each request. This means the regional processing location may differ from the data center region specified on a customer’s order form.

### Enable Sensitive Data Redaction for emails
ServiceNow provides an out-of-the-box plugin called Sensitive Data Redaction for Inbound Emails, which customer admins can install. This plugin allows customers to redact sensitive data, such as Social Security numbers, financial information, email addresses, phone numbers. Collaborate with stakeholders to determine if the organization should install and configure the Sensitive Data Redaction plugin to automatically mask sensitive information in inbound emails.

---

November 2025 | Release: Zurich  
34
```

## Security_Admin role
[High Security Settings](https://www.servicenow.com) and the [High Security plugin](https://www.servicenow.com) are activated by default on new ServiceNow instances and they can provide an elevated privilege role called `security_admin` role. This role allows users to create and change access controls and change High Security Settings. In the base system, only the default System Administrator (admin) user has the `security_admin` role. The customer admin should work with stakeholders, such as the company’s security team, to determine if an elevated role assignment is required. The `security_admin` role should be assigned to a limited number of users and groups.

## Best practice prioritization
Customers should evaluate each best practice in collaboration with relevant stakeholders to determine applicability and evaluate potential risks. Therefore, they must work closely with security and compliance teams when identifying the best practices to address.

Customers can also allow low-privileged users to authenticate with an email one-time password (OTP) or a short message service (SMS) OTP. These methods are easy to use and require minimal setup.

## Security contacts

**Customer responsibility**  
As outlined in the DSA, customers are responsible for identifying and maintaining appropriate security contacts by identifying them in [ServiceNow Support Security Contacts](https://www.servicenow.com).

**Best practices**  

### Create a process to update security contacts regularly  
Ensure the security contact record within ServiceNow Support is always kept up to date, with details of at least two appropriate information security personnel. Set a reminder to review the security contact details at least quarterly to ensure they are current and accurate.  

- Security contacts should be authorized to act on the information they receive, because it may be critically important to the organization.  
- Use a distribution list in the security contact field when possible.  

**Additional information**  
- Update your [ServiceNow Support Security Contacts](https://www.servicenow.com) (requires a ServiceNow Support account)

---

### Key ownership and control
Customers need to determine which type of encryption key they will use on the ServiceNow AI Platform: a ServiceNow-managed key (SMK) or bring your own key (BYOK).

### Encryption key lifecycle management
- **Generation**: When using BYOK, keys should be generated in accordance with the company’s internal security policy and follow the [ServiceNow key preparation guidance](https://example.com).
- **Rotation**: Customers should regularly rotate keys to minimize exposure. ServiceNow supports scheduled rotation for SMK and provides notification reminders for BYOK.
- **Storage**: BYOK’s should be stored in a secure, protected environment that performs regular backups to ensure that the keys remain available and recoverable, if needed.

---

## Best practices

It is recommended that customers limit the use of personal identities for executing unattended automations or integrations. By implementing ServiceNow access policy restrictions to clearly separate these data flows, organizations can better define and uphold policies aligned with their identity architecture.

### Use security attributes when possible
Customers should utilize applicable security attributes when possible. Security attributes offer an alternative method for access control via role definitions.

### Use security data filters when possible
Security data filters enable access restriction to records based on a user’s role, or other security attribute-related assertions. Security data filters are applied before a query is executed and ensure only authorized users can view records regardless of how data is accessed. Customers should explicitly enable security data filters for user-facing queries that are not using GlideRecordSecure.

# RECOVER

## Business continuity and disaster recovery

### Customer responsibility
While ServiceNow manages infrastructure-level disaster recovery and system failover, customers should create and maintain business continuity and disaster recovery plans tailored to their processes and risk tolerance for their ServiceNow instance. This plan should include developing internal communication and response strategies.

By proactively addressing these responsibilities, customers help ensure their organization is prepared to respond quickly and effectively in the event of an unexpected disruption.

### ServiceNow responsibility
ServiceNow operates a disaster recovery program for customer instances called the [Information System Contingency Plan (ISCP)](https://www.servicenow.com/). (Link requires access to the ServiceNow CORE Compliance Portal. Find out how to access CORE [here](https://www.servicenow.com/).)

## Understand how to review logs for investigations
One of the most important components of incident response is ServiceNow instance logs. These [system logs](https://support.servicenow.com), will be able to provide customers’ security teams with the necessary telemetry for their incident response investigations. Logs can be reviewed using a variety of methods, such as the [log file browser](https://support.servicenow.com), Table APIs, and directly in the platform.

## Conduct postmortem activities following a security incident
Following a security incident, it is important to perform a postmortem review of the investigations to determine possible improvements that can be made for future incident response activities. This can include identifying possible communication issues, gaps within the environment’s security posture, and ensuring all involved parties understand the root cause of the issue and how to avoid similar situations moving forward.

### Review event logs to detect unauthorized access and privilege escalation
Regularly review event logs for login activity and privilege escalation to identify and respond to potential security threats. Event logs provide insights into system activity, including successful and failed login attempts and privilege escalation events.

### Monitor system logs for configuration changes and errors
Routinely monitor system logs to detect configuration changes, system errors, and unusual data connections that may indicate security or operational issues. System logs contain information about general activity, including configuration changes, system errors, workflows, and inbound/outbound data connections.

### Review transaction logs to detect malicious web activity
Review transaction logs to identify unusual or malicious web activity, as they provide records of all browser-based interactions with the ServiceNow instance.

---

### ServiceNow responsibility
ServiceNow operates a Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) system to review and correlate logs from multiple network and infrastructure sources. A Scheduled Security Operations Checklist is in place, which includes daily reviews of:
- Linux and Windows systems  
- Network devices  
- Intrusion Detection System (IDS) alerts  
- Behavioral and identified issue logs  

High-risk issues, such as intrusion detection events, trigger real-time alerts that are immediately sent to the Security Incident Response Team for review. Network and infrastructure log events are retained for a minimum of 90 days.

---

### Best practices

### Harden the MID Server and operating system
Deploy and secure the MID Server’s operating system and runtime environment according to your organization’s IT security policies. Use only [supported operating systems](#) that receive security updates. The MID Server Java application runs on supported Windows or Linux servers with a Java Runtime Environment.

### Harden server and operating system for MID Server security
Ensure that the server operating system and runtime environment are deployed, secured, and hardened in accordance with the organization’s established internal IT security policies and operational procedures. Operate only on supported operating systems that continue to receive security updates. The MID Server Java application runs on supported Windows or Linux Servers with a Java Runtime Environment.

Establish and follow a routine schedule to promptly install security patches and platform updates in both production and sub-production environments. Treat production and sub-production systems with equal diligence, ensuring that all environments are updated.

ServiceNow releases two major version updates per year and only supports the current version (N) and one prior release (N-1).

Instances operating on older family releases are categorized as “End-of-Life” (EOL) and do not receive new updates or patches. Organizations should establish and maintain a formal process to proactively track their ServiceNow instance’s family release version, ensuring timely upgrades before the platform reaches EOL status.

<DOCUMENT>## Adopt a proactive patch management process
Establish and follow a routine schedule to promptly install security patches and platform updates in both production and sub-production environments. Treat production and sub-production systems with equal diligence, ensuring that all environments are updated.

## Ensure instances remain on a supported family release
ServiceNow releases two major version updates per year and only supports the current version (N) and one prior release (N-1).

Instances operating on older family releases are categorized as “End-of-Life” (EOL) and do not receive new updates or patches. Organizations should establish and maintain a formal process to proactively track their ServiceNow instance’s family release version, ensuring timely upgrades before the platform reaches EOL status.

---

<DOCUMENT>#### Align with change management

Customers should work with all stakeholders to define appropriate usage guidelines for ServiceNow. This guidance should be published in the organizational standards, when appropriate. Manage instance activity in accordance with company guidelines throughout each instance’s lifecycle.

#### Retire unused instances
Decommission ServiceNow instances that are no longer needed, following the organization’s documented retirement process that includes backing up critical data, removing all integrations and credentials, and updating the centralized inventory to reflect changes.

```markdown
# Encryption
## Data in transit

### Customer responsibility
The ServiceNow AI Platform provides customers with encryption in transit via HTTPS for user access and API access to the instance. The platform also supports several protocols for integration with customer or third-party systems, including HTTPS, LDAPS, FTPS, and SCP. Customers should configure data in transit encryption methods in accordance with their security policies and use cases.

---

### ServiceNow responsibility
The ServiceNow AI Platform supports default encryption in transit for sessions inbound to the instance using a minimum of TLS 1.2. All attempted access to a ServiceNow instance over HTTP is redirected to HTTPS.

ServiceNow instance email infrastructure supports opportunistic TLS for sending or receiving email.

---

### Best practices

#### Enforce TLS 1.2 or higher for browser connections
Customer admins should configure their web browsers to use only TLS 1.2, or higher when connecting to their ServiceNow instance.

question: What is the primary means of restoring service in case of a disruption?

sentences:
If the infrastructure hosting the currently active instance experiences a disruption, ServiceNow activates a failover process that transfers customer operations to the unaffected colocation facility. In this model, the targeted recovery point objective (RPO) and recovery time objective (RTO) durations are one and two hours, respectively.

### Backups
The ServiceNow [Advanced High Availability (AHA)](https://www.servicenow.com/) architecture is the primary means to restore service in the case of a disruption that could impact availability; however, ServiceNow also performs backups of each customer’s instance(s).

In specific scenarios, using more traditional data backup and recovery mechanisms may be appropriate.

Backups are stored in the same colocation facilities where the data resides, with production instances backed up in both colocation facilities in the pair.

---

### ServiceNow responsibility
As the data processor, ServiceNow supports the data controllers by providing features to enable access and control of data processing activities and obligations.

ServiceNow has a dedicated Cloud Assurance team responsible for several governance and compliance efforts across the organization, including managing the ServiceNow compliance program. ServiceNow is reviewed on an annual basis by independent third-party auditors. ServiceNow will establish and maintain sufficient controls to meet certification and attestation for the objectives stated in ISO/IEC 27001, 27017, 27018, 27701, 9001, 22301, 42001 (new AI/IT), and SSAE 18 SOC 2 Type 2 (or equivalent standards) for the security program.

---

### Best practices

#### Clarify stakeholder data responsibilities
Set up a process to regularly involve stakeholders in defining data responsibilities, making sure that controls meet internal policies and goals and are working as intended.

To enhance threat detection and response, organizations should actively monitor and forward relevant log data from their ServiceNow instance to a SIEM following internal security policies.

Customers should ensure the Protected Tables plugin is enabled on their ServiceNow instance and the protection levels are set. When the `com.glide.security.protected_table.enabled` property is set to true, the protected tables plugin will be used to prevent higher privilege users on an instance from tampering with log tables. Collaborate with the organization’s security team to review and set appropriate protection levels and actions and add specific alerts that may need to be added to monitoring procedures.

question: Which systems and devices are included in the daily reviews of the Security Operations Checklist?

sentences:

|------------------------------------------------|----------|------------|----------------------|
| Security contact details                       | ●        | ●          |                      |
| Data management and privacy compliance         | ●        | ●          |                      |

Mid Securty Centers Securely Down Legacy LFTWARE

---

### ServiceNow responsibility
ServiceNow operates a Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) system to review and correlate logs from multiple network and infrastructure sources. A Scheduled Security Operations Checklist is in place, which includes daily reviews of:
- Linux and Windows systems  
- Network devices  
- Intrusion Detection System (IDS) alerts  
- Behavioral and identified issue logs  

High-risk issues, such as intrusion detection events, trigger real-time alerts that are immediately sent to the Security Incident Response Team for review. Network and infrastructure log events are retained for a minimum of 90 days.

---

### Best practices

It is recommended that customers limit the use of personal identities for executing unattended automations or integrations. By implementing ServiceNow access policy restrictions to clearly separate these data flows, organizations can better define and uphold policies aligned with their identity architecture.

### Use security attributes when possible
Customers should utilize applicable security attributes when possible. Security attributes offer an alternative method for access control via role definitions.

### Use security data filters when possible
Security data filters enable access restriction to records based on a user’s role, or other security attribute-related assertions. Security data filters are applied before a query is executed and ensure only authorized users can view records regardless of how data is accessed. Customers should explicitly enable security data filters for user-facing queries that are not using GlideRecordSecure.

The key differences include accountability (individual vs system), licensing, authentication, and lifecycle management. Both require strict least privilege, but non-interactive accounts need extra controls like credential rotation, monitoring for unusual API activity, and clear ownership documentation to prevent unauthorized system access.

For integration accounts, enable the web services access flag to prevent those accounts from using interactive sessions.

### Define roles clearly
Identify each job function that will interact with the ServiceNow AI Platform and assign specific user roles with clear names and descriptions. Update roles as business needs evolve and communicate privileges to users. Adopt the concept of least-privileged access. This ensures effective access control and simplifies auditing.

```markdown
# Authorization

## Customer responsibility
Customers are responsible for defining user roles based on job functions and assigning appropriate permissions using role-based access control (RBAC) and access control lists (ACLs). It is recommended to configure ACLs to enforce the principle of least privilege and use non-production instances to test changes before deployment.

---

## Best practices

### Distinguish between interactive vs non-interactive user accounts
**Interactive user accounts** should use MFA and role-based access controls, ensuring least privilege and tying actions to individuals for accountability.

**Non-interactive accounts**, intended for integrations and automation, should authenticate via API keys or OAuth tokens, have roles restricted to their purpose, utilize IP restrictions when possible, and link actions to the system or team.

#### Address noncompliance with security hardening and hardening compliance score
Use [Security hardening](https://www.servicenow.com) to identify, test, and assess noncompliance in a sub-production instance. Review the hardening compliance score to determine how closely your instance aligns with SSC hardening recommendations.

*Note: A high compliance score does not guarantee that the instance is fully secure—it only reflects alignment with SSC hardening settings.*

#### Run Security Center security scans regularly
The [Security scanner](https://www.servicenow.com) helps discover and correct access control misconfigurations. Use the Security Scanner built-in to SSC to scan your instance against a set of security checks in order to identify misconfigurations on a regular cadence.

#### Configure and enforce strong password policies
It is important for customers to set password policies for their Identity Provider (IdP) and within their ServiceNow instance(s). This includes specifying requirements like minimum password length, complexity, expiration, uniqueness, and lockout conditions for native accounts. Also, be sure configurations meet your organizational standards.

#### Enable account lockout to prevent brute force attacks
As a critical security best practice, customers should enable account lockouts both on their IdP and for all local accounts within the ServiceNow instance. This measure is essential to defend against brute force authentication attacks by automatically locking accounts after a set number of failed login attempts.

## Security_Admin role
[High Security Settings](https://www.servicenow.com) and the [High Security plugin](https://www.servicenow.com) are activated by default on new ServiceNow instances and they can provide an elevated privilege role called `security_admin` role. This role allows users to create and change access controls and change High Security Settings. In the base system, only the default System Administrator (admin) user has the `security_admin` role. The customer admin should work with stakeholders, such as the company’s security team, to determine if an elevated role assignment is required. The `security_admin` role should be assigned to a limited number of users and groups.

## Best practice prioritization
Customers should evaluate each best practice in collaboration with relevant stakeholders to determine applicability and evaluate potential risks. Therefore, they must work closely with security and compliance teams when identifying the best practices to address.

ServiceNow provides the current versions of these addenda on [Legal: Customer Agreements and Terms](https://www.servicenow.com) for general understanding; however, to understand the specific details, administrators are advised to reach out to their own compliance or legal support team.  

---

### Best practices  

#### Review and understand the DSA and DPA terms and conditions  
Consult with your compliance and legal teams to ensure they have read and understand the ServiceNow DSA and/or DPA.  

#### Where applicable, review the ServiceNow third party hosted product addendum  
Work with compliance and legal teams to address any questions regarding the use of ServiceNow subscription products that use data hosting provided by third-party sub-processors (third party hosted products).  

---

```markdown
# Authorization

## Customer responsibility
Customers are responsible for defining user roles based on job functions and assigning appropriate permissions using role-based access control (RBAC) and access control lists (ACLs). It is recommended to configure ACLs to enforce the principle of least privilege and use non-production instances to test changes before deployment.

---

## Best practices

### Distinguish between interactive vs non-interactive user accounts
**Interactive user accounts** should use MFA and role-based access controls, ensuring least privilege and tying actions to individuals for accountability.

**Non-interactive accounts**, intended for integrations and automation, should authenticate via API keys or OAuth tokens, have roles restricted to their purpose, utilize IP restrictions when possible, and link actions to the system or team.

#### Periodically review the ServiceNow Customer Security Portal
Establish a process to conduct regular reviews of the Customer Security Portal, including compliance certifications, security advisories, Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs), SOC reports, and instance security best practices. Whether evaluating ServiceNow as a vendor or seeking guidance on instance security, this portal serves as a centralized resource for all ServiceNow security needs.

---

- [Higher Education Community Vendor Assessment Toolkit (HECVAT)](#)
- [Standardized Information Gathering (SIG) questionnaire](#)

S/MIME is an end-to-end encryption protocol for sending digitally signed and encrypted emails, ensuring data confidentiality, authenticity, and integrity. Collaborate with stakeholders to determine if this feature should be configured.

## Establish a regular access review process for Access Analyzer reports
Customers should establish processes to perform regular reviews of the reports to ensure that only authorized personnel have appropriate access:
- Define a review cadence (e.g., quarterly) for auditing access reports.

- Generate and retain reports regularly to support audit, compliance, and governance activities.

# Encryption
## Data in transit

### Customer responsibility
The ServiceNow AI Platform provides customers with encryption in transit via HTTPS for user access and API access to the instance. The platform also supports several protocols for integration with customer or third-party systems, including HTTPS, LDAPS, FTPS, and SCP. Customers should configure data in transit encryption methods in accordance with their security policies and use cases.

---

### ServiceNow responsibility
The ServiceNow AI Platform supports default encryption in transit for sessions inbound to the instance using a minimum of TLS 1.2. All attempted access to a ServiceNow instance over HTTP is redirected to HTTPS.

ServiceNow instance email infrastructure supports opportunistic TLS for sending or receiving email.

---

### Best practices

#### Enforce TLS 1.2 or higher for browser connections
Customer admins should configure their web browsers to use only TLS 1.2, or higher when connecting to their ServiceNow instance.

# Data at rest

## Customer responsibility
Data at rest encryption is not enabled by default for customers using the standard ServiceNow Commercial Cloud.

To meet organizational security and compliance requirements, customers must evaluate and implement appropriate encryption solutions for their ServiceNow instance(s).

ServiceNow offers a range of encryption options, including free [Field Encryption Starter](https://example.com) and premium solutions such as [Cloud Encryption (CE)](https://example.com) and [Full Disk Encryption (FDE)](https://example.com), which are available at an additional cost.

Customers are also responsible for key lifecycle management through the [Key Management Framework (KMF)](https://example.com). The KMF introduces specific roles for cryptographic modules and key management operations. Customer admins should review these roles and assign them in accordance with their company’s internal security policy.

The assessment typically spans several months and follows an iterative process where findings are remediated by ServiceNow security and development teams. Results of these penetration tests are available to customers and prospects under NDA via the ServiceNow CORE Compliance Portal.

## Best practices

### Create a process to examine ServiceNow penetration test reports periodically
Create a process to ensure stakeholders, such as your security team, review the most recent published [ServiceNow penetration test reports](#) on the ServiceNow CORE Compliance Portal. Find out how to access CORE [here](#).

```markdown
# RESPOND

## Incident management

### Customer responsibility
During an incident, customers must lead investigations based on their internal processes, security needs, and regulatory obligations, as ServiceNow cannot anticipate these specifics. In addition, ServiceNow asks that customers keep their security contacts updated in the event that ServiceNow needs to reach out for a suspected incident.

While ServiceNow can assist with questions on the investigation, customers are responsible for classifying related behavior as malicious or benign, given their contextual knowledge. [ServiceNow Support](#) can help interpret log samples but cannot review all logs or determine the full scope of an incident.

To ensure effective assistance, customers are responsible for providing detailed information—such as timelines, IPs, and user data—when requesting support. Broad log queries can delay investigations, whereas targeted data enables faster resolution.

### Monitor antivirus queues for malicious uploads
Customers should establish a defined process for monitoring uploaded file attachments for potential malicious content, leveraging anti-virus scanning capabilities in the platform. This process should include ongoing collaboration with security teams to analyze, identify, and respond to emerging patterns or trends in suspicious uploads, ensuring proactive protection of the instance and its data.

### Configure inbound REST API rate limiting
Set rules to limit inbound REST API requests. Customers can create rules that limit the number of inbound REST API requests processed per hour and can also create rules to limit requests for specific users, users with specific roles, or all users.

### Review public REST API endpoints
Review the identified REST API endpoint and use cases. Determine if unauthenticated users should be allowed access.

## Incident management

### Customer responsibility
During an incident, customers must lead investigations based on their internal processes, security needs, and regulatory obligations, as ServiceNow cannot anticipate these specifics. In addition, ServiceNow asks that customers keep their security contacts updated in the event that ServiceNow needs to reach out for a suspected incident.

While ServiceNow can assist with questions on the investigation, customers are responsible for classifying related behavior as malicious or benign, given their contextual knowledge. [ServiceNow Support](#) can help interpret log samples but cannot review all logs or determine the full scope of an incident.

To ensure effective assistance, customers are responsible for providing detailed information—such as timelines, IPs, and user data—when requesting support. Broad log queries can delay investigations, whereas targeted data enables faster resolution.</DOCUMENT>
<DOCUMENT>### Monitor antivirus queues for malicious uploads
Customers should establish a defined process for monitoring uploaded file attachments for potential malicious content, leveraging anti-virus scanning capabilities in the platform. This process should include ongoing collaboration with security teams to analyze, identify, and respond to emerging patterns or trends in suspicious uploads, ensuring proactive protection of the instance and its data.

### Configure inbound REST API rate limiting
Set rules to limit inbound REST API requests. Customers can create rules that limit the number of inbound REST API requests processed per hour and can also create rules to limit requests for specific users, users with specific roles, or all users.

### Review public REST API endpoints
Review the identified REST API endpoint and use cases. Determine if unauthenticated users should be allowed access.</DOCUMENT>

# IDENTIFY

## Instance management

### Customer responsibility
Customers must oversee all the organization’s production and sub-production ServiceNow instances, ensuring each one’s purpose, owner, and data classification are known.

### Best practices

#### Maintain a centralized inventory of instances
Maintain a centralized, up-to-date inventory of all ServiceNow instances (see the [ServiceNow Support Instances Dashboard](#)). Clearly identify each instance by name and URL, environment type (such as Production, Development, Test, or Sandbox), business purpose, designated business and technical owners, and data classification.

#### Regularly review all instances
Conduct regular reviews of all production and sub-production ServiceNow instances to verify each instance’s ownership, purpose, and ongoing alignment with business needs. Document each review and its findings and formalize the follow-up process to support continuous oversight.

## Understand the difference between Allow-If and Deny-Unless ACLs
Allow-If allows access upon successful evaluation and is the default ACL. Deny-Unless denies access unless there is a successful evaluation. Deny-Unless ACLs will take priority against Allow-If ACLs in ACL Evaluation as it will be evaluated first. The Deny-Unless ACL defines the users that will NOT be denied. Said another way, the user will be denied access unless the role, condition, and script requirements are met.

## Verify Security Jump Start—ACL Rules Plugin is enabled
All new ServiceNow instances have the [Security Jump Start—ACL Rules plugin](#) installed to provide a base level of access security for key system tables. Use this plugin to establish foundational ACL protections for sensitive system data.

question: What does the `security_admin` role allow users to do?

sentences:
## Security_Admin role
[High Security Settings](https://www.servicenow.com) and the [High Security plugin](https://www.servicenow.com) are activated by default on new ServiceNow instances and they can provide an elevated privilege role called `security_admin` role. This role allows users to create and change access controls and change High Security Settings. In the base system, only the default System Administrator (admin) user has the `security_admin` role. The customer admin should work with stakeholders, such as the company’s security team, to determine if an elevated role assignment is required. The `security_admin` role should be assigned to a limited number of users and groups.

## Best practice prioritization
Customers should evaluate each best practice in collaboration with relevant stakeholders to determine applicability and evaluate potential risks. Therefore, they must work closely with security and compliance teams when identifying the best practices to address.

## Adopt a proactive patch management process
Establish and follow a routine schedule to promptly install security patches and platform updates in both production and sub-production environments. Treat production and sub-production systems with equal diligence, ensuring that all environments are updated.

## Ensure instances remain on a supported family release
ServiceNow releases two major version updates per year and only supports the current version (N) and one prior release (N-1).

Instances operating on older family releases are categorized as “End-of-Life” (EOL) and do not receive new updates or patches. Organizations should establish and maintain a formal process to proactively track their ServiceNow instance’s family release version, ensuring timely upgrades before the platform reaches EOL status.

# The Shared Responsibility Model

Security is a partnership between ServiceNow and the customer, both with specific responsibilities. Therefore, it is essential that each party understands their role in this partnership. Using the extensive capabilities of the ServiceNow AI Platform, customers can configure instances to meet their unique security policies and obligations while also complying with any regional or industry-specific requirements.

- **As the data controller**, the customer determines access rights to their instance and the data it contains. Security controls within the instance enable customers to implement policies appropriate to their own requirements and make decisions on data classification.

- **As the data processor**, ServiceNow secures the platform infrastructure and provides tools for security management and monitoring according to customer requirements.

The key differences include accountability (individual vs system), licensing, authentication, and lifecycle management. Both require strict least privilege, but non-interactive accounts need extra controls like credential rotation, monitoring for unusual API activity, and clear ownership documentation to prevent unauthorized system access.

For integration accounts, enable the web services access flag to prevent those accounts from using interactive sessions.

### Define roles clearly
Identify each job function that will interact with the ServiceNow AI Platform and assign specific user roles with clear names and descriptions. Update roles as business needs evolve and communicate privileges to users. Adopt the concept of least-privileged access. This ensures effective access control and simplifies auditing.

- Log history  
- Auditing

- Syslog probe  
- Avoid Log Tampering  
- Data retention, rotation, cleanup and instance size  
  *(requires a ServiceNow Support account)*  
- Enable protected tables plugin  
- MID Server command audit log  
- REST and SOAP request (Outbound web services: Logging)  
- API Analytics

Using the extensive capabilities of the ServiceNow AI Platform, customers can configure instances to meet their unique security policies and obligations while also complying with any regional or industry-specific requirements.

- **As the data controller**, the customer determines access rights to their instance and the data it contains. Security controls within the instance enable customers to implement policies appropriate to their own requirements and make decisions on data classification.

- **As the data processor**, ServiceNow secures the platform infrastructure and provides tools for security management and monitoring according to customer requirements.</DOCUMENT>
<DOCUMENT>The key differences include accountability (individual vs system), licensing, authentication, and lifecycle management. Both require strict least privilege, but non-interactive accounts need extra controls like credential rotation, monitoring for unusual API activity, and clear ownership documentation to prevent unauthorized system access.

For integration accounts, enable the web services access flag to prevent those accounts from using interactive sessions.

### Define roles clearly
Identify each job function that will interact with the ServiceNow AI Platform and assign specific user roles with clear names and descriptions. Update roles as business needs evolve and communicate privileges to users. Adopt the concept of least-privileged access. This ensures effective access control and simplifies auditing.</DOCUMENT>

### ServiceNow responsibility
ServiceNow, as the data processor, supports customer incident response by querying backend logs upon request, subject to an eight-week retention limit. While customers are responsible for interpreting logs, [ServiceNow Support](#) can help review samples to clarify log types. However, it is essential to note that ServiceNow Support does not have the resources to analyze every event.

ServiceNow Support and security teams assist in identifying possible causes of incidents and offer preventive guidance, though recommendations may be limited by platform capabilities.

At an enterprise level, security teams at ServiceNow have implemented detection rules that initiate internal incident response processes. Detections related to customer instances are normally reported through a support case.

### Best practices

It is recommended that customers limit the use of personal identities for executing unattended automations or integrations. By implementing ServiceNow access policy restrictions to clearly separate these data flows, organizations can better define and uphold policies aligned with their identity architecture.

### Use security attributes when possible
Customers should utilize applicable security attributes when possible. Security attributes offer an alternative method for access control via role definitions.

### Use security data filters when possible
Security data filters enable access restriction to records based on a user’s role, or other security attribute-related assertions. Security data filters are applied before a query is executed and ensure only authorized users can view records regardless of how data is accessed. Customers should explicitly enable security data filters for user-facing queries that are not using GlideRecordSecure.

### Key ownership and control
Customers need to determine which type of encryption key they will use on the ServiceNow AI Platform: a ServiceNow-managed key (SMK) or bring your own key (BYOK).

### Encryption key lifecycle management
- **Generation**: When using BYOK, keys should be generated in accordance with the company’s internal security policy and follow the [ServiceNow key preparation guidance](https://example.com).
- **Rotation**: Customers should regularly rotate keys to minimize exposure. ServiceNow supports scheduled rotation for SMK and provides notification reminders for BYOK.
- **Storage**: BYOK’s should be stored in a secure, protected environment that performs regular backups to ensure that the keys remain available and recoverable, if needed.

# Best practices continued

## Enforce email authentication and domain restrictions
Customers can control what domains and users are allowed to send email into their ServiceNow instance, as well as what domains and users are valid email destinations using system address filters. Collaborate with your security and IT teams to determine if you need to configure any of the following email controls.

ServiceNow provides Sender Policy Framework (SPF) records to identify email hosts that are approved to send as ServiceNow. To use SPF services, the customer’s email systems must be configured to accept mail from the ServiceNow email infrastructure. ServiceNow recommends that customers consume the published ServiceNow SPF records dynamically, rather than allowing by IP address. When allowing by IP address, it is important to note that the addresses may change.

#### Align with change management
Changes to ServiceNow instances should follow the organization’s change management process. Document each activity with an official record and obtain approvals before proceeding to ensure tracking, authorization, and compliance.

#### Plan for acceptable use
Customers should work with all stakeholders to define appropriate usage guidelines for ServiceNow. This guidance should be published in the organizational standards, when appropriate. Manage instance activity in accordance with company guidelines throughout each instance’s lifecycle.

#### Retire unused instances
Decommission ServiceNow instances that are no longer needed, following the organization’s documented retirement process that includes backing up critical data, removing all integrations and credentials, and updating the centralized inventory to reflect changes.

sentences:
---

## ServiceNow responsibility

ServiceNow is committed to building and deploying AI responsibly. Our generative AI solutions are designed with human-centric principles, ensuring customers remain in control.

ServiceNow maintains documented AI governance policies and standard procedures that incorporate industry best practices, including AI data governance, dataset lifecycle management, AI development, and deployment. These policies are regularly updated to address emerging technologies, evolving industry standards, and new security threats.

The ServiceNow AI governance process aligns with the NIST Risk Management Framework for AI and complies with all applicable local laws and regulations. As regulations evolve, we continue to adopt, expand, and align with relevant compliance programs to ensure ongoing adherence.

### Determine if your organization requires penetration testing of an instance
As a security best practice, organizations should collaborate with security and compliance teams to identify which ServiceNow instances require penetration testing and establish a clear process for these assessments. This procedure should be reviewed regularly to ensure it remains aligned with evolving security requirements and organizational needs, allowing timely updates if the scope of testing or risk profile changes.

sentences:
#### Configure and enforce strong password policies
It is important for customers to set password policies for their Identity Provider (IdP) and within their ServiceNow instance(s). This includes specifying requirements like minimum password length, complexity, expiration, uniqueness, and lockout conditions for native accounts. Also, be sure configurations meet your organizational standards.

#### Enable account lockout to prevent brute force attacks
As a critical security best practice, customers should enable account lockouts both on their IdP and for all local accounts within the ServiceNow instance. This measure is essential to defend against brute force authentication attacks by automatically locking accounts after a set number of failed login attempts.

## ServiceNow responsibility

ServiceNow is committed to building and deploying AI responsibly. Our generative AI solutions are designed with human-centric principles, ensuring customers remain in control.

ServiceNow maintains documented AI governance policies and standard procedures that incorporate industry best practices, including AI data governance, dataset lifecycle management, AI development, and deployment. The customer’s security team should work with stakeholders to thoroughly assess the regulatory and organizational requirements for data stored in their ServiceNow instance(s) to determine if data at rest needs to be encrypted.

When implementing the chosen encryption method, ensure encryption settings and key management are configured in accordance with internal policies and compliance standards to safeguard sensitive information throughout its lifecycle.

Logs can be reviewed using a variety of methods, such as the [log file browser](https://support.servicenow.com), Table APIs, and directly in the platform.

Following a security incident, it is important to perform a postmortem review of the investigations to determine possible improvements that can be made for future incident response activities. <DOCUMENT>#### Configure and enforce strong password policies
It is important for customers to set password policies for their Identity Provider (IdP) and within their ServiceNow instance(s). This includes specifying requirements like minimum password length, complexity, expiration, uniqueness, and lockout conditions for native accounts. Also, be sure configurations meet your organizational standards.

#### Enable account lockout to prevent brute force attacks
As a critical security best practice, customers should enable account lockouts both on their IdP and for all local accounts within the ServiceNow instance. This measure is essential to defend against brute force authentication attacks by automatically locking accounts after a set number of failed login attempts.</DOCUMENT>
<DOCUMENT>---

## ServiceNow responsibility

ServiceNow is committed to building and deploying AI responsibly. Our generative AI solutions are designed with human-centric principles, ensuring customers remain in control.

ServiceNow maintains documented AI governance policies and standard procedures that incorporate industry best practices, including AI data governance, dataset lifecycle management, AI development, and deployment. These policies are regularly updated to address emerging technologies, evolving industry standards, and new security threats.

The ServiceNow AI governance process aligns with the NIST Risk Management Framework for AI and complies with all applicable local laws and regulations. As regulations evolve, we continue to adopt, expand, and align with relevant compliance programs to ensure ongoing adherence.</DOCUMENT>
<DOCUMENT>---

## Best practices

### Choose an encryption method for data at rest in an instance*
The customer’s security team should work with stakeholders to thoroughly assess the regulatory and organizational requirements for data stored in their ServiceNow instance(s) to determine if data at rest needs to be encrypted.

Based on this assessment, customers should select the most appropriate encryption method offered by ServiceNow. When implementing the chosen encryption method, ensure encryption settings and key management are configured in accordance with internal policies and compliance standards to safeguard sensitive information throughout its lifecycle.

### Customers seeking included functionality
**Field Encryption Starter**:  
Data stored within a ServiceNow instance can be protected with Field Encryption Starter, which allows customers to encrypt specific fields within the instance using AES128 or AES256 encryption.</DOCUMENT>
<DOCUMENT>## Understand how to review logs for investigations
One of the most important components of incident response is ServiceNow instance logs. These [system logs](https://support.servicenow.com), will be able to provide customers’ security teams with the necessary telemetry for their incident response investigations. Logs can be reviewed using a variety of methods, such as the [log file browser](https://support.servicenow.com), Table APIs, and directly in the platform.

## Conduct postmortem activities following a security incident
Following a security incident, it is important to perform a postmortem review of the investigations to determine possible improvements that can be made for future incident response activities. This can include identifying possible communication issues, gaps within the environment’s security posture, and ensuring all involved parties understand the root cause of the issue and how to avoid similar situations moving forward.

## Data in transit

### Customer responsibility
The ServiceNow AI Platform provides customers with encryption in transit via HTTPS for user access and API access to the instance. The platform also supports several protocols for integration with customer or third-party systems, including HTTPS, LDAPS, FTPS, and SCP. Customers should configure data in transit encryption methods in accordance with their security policies and use cases.

---

### ServiceNow responsibility
The ServiceNow AI Platform supports default encryption in transit for sessions inbound to the instance using a minimum of TLS 1.2. All attempted access to a ServiceNow instance over HTTP is redirected to HTTPS.

ServiceNow instance email infrastructure supports opportunistic TLS for sending or receiving email.

---

### Best practices

#### Enforce TLS 1.2 or higher for browser connections

### Monitor antivirus queues for malicious uploads
Customers should establish a defined process for monitoring uploaded file attachments for potential malicious content, leveraging anti-virus scanning capabilities in the platform. This process should include ongoing collaboration with security teams to analyze, identify, and respond to emerging patterns or trends in suspicious uploads, ensuring proactive protection of the instance and its data.

### Configure inbound REST API rate limiting
Set rules to limit inbound REST API requests. Customers can create rules that limit the number of inbound REST API requests processed per hour and can also create rules to limit requests for specific users, users with specific roles, or all users.

### Review public REST API endpoints
Review the identified REST API endpoint and use cases. Determine if unauthenticated users should be allowed access.

### Enable table auditing for complete record history
Customers can enable auditing for database tables, making record history perpetual and allowing tracking of any changes made to the data since creation. By default, only the incident, problem, and change tables are tracked. For other tables, auditing must be enabled manually.

### Review import logs to ensure data integrity
Regularly review import logs to track data import activity, including source, status, and timing, to ensure data integrity and detect any anomalies.

### Use API Analytics to track inbound API usage
Use API Analytics to monitor inbound API usage and users. Customers can track and analyze inbound REST and SOAP activity with API Analytics. These analytics help customers understand which APIs are being used, by whom, and to what degree.

sentences:
- **The colocation facility** and the third-party **cloud service provider** (CSP) also have shared responsibilities with the data controller (customer) and data processor (ServiceNow).

For more information about security responsibilities concerning customer data, see the [ServiceNow Shared Responsibility Model overview](#).

This document includes shared responsibilities specified at the beginning of each section. Customers should review each customer responsibility with relevant stakeholders to ensure the organization fully understands its obligations as specified in the ServiceNow Shared Responsibility Model. Relevant stakeholders may include architecture teams, security teams, and compliance personnel.

It is recommended that customers limit the use of personal identities for executing unattended automations or integrations. By implementing ServiceNow access policy restrictions to clearly separate these data flows, organizations can better define and uphold policies aligned with their identity architecture.

### Use security attributes when possible
Customers should utilize applicable security attributes when possible. Security attributes offer an alternative method for access control via role definitions.

### Use security data filters when possible
Security data filters enable access restriction to records based on a user’s role, or other security attribute-related assertions. Security data filters are applied before a query is executed and ensure only authorized users can view records regardless of how data is accessed. Customers should explicitly enable security data filters for user-facing queries that are not using GlideRecordSecure.

Customers can control what domains and users are allowed to send email into their ServiceNow instance, as well as what domains and users are valid email destinations using system address filters. ### Configure inbound REST API rate limiting
Set rules to limit inbound REST API requests. Customers can create rules that limit the number of inbound REST API requests processed per hour and can also create rules to limit requests for specific users, users with specific roles, or all users.

### Review public REST API endpoints
Review the identified REST API endpoint and use cases. Determine if unauthenticated users should be allowed access.</DOCUMENT>

sentences:

## Best practices continued

### Monitor and forward logs to the organization’s SIEM for threat detection
To enhance threat detection and response, organizations should actively monitor and forward relevant log data from their ServiceNow instance to a SIEM following internal security policies.

### Enable Protected Tables plugin to manage log tampering
Customers should ensure the Protected Tables plugin is enabled on their ServiceNow instance and the protection levels are set. When the `com.glide.security.protected_table.enabled` property is set to true, the protected tables plugin will be used to prevent higher privilege users on an instance from tampering with log tables. Collaborate with the organization’s security team to review and set appropriate protection levels and actions and add specific alerts that may need to be added to monitoring procedures.

- **Scan comparison:** Compare two scans from the same security suite and view results in a dashboard.
- **Scan checks:** Identify issues and implement security recommendations for your organization.
- **Custom scan suites:** Create and schedule custom suites to analyze your instance’s security posture.
- **Scan findings:** Identify records that violated rules, locate the source record, and review the number of times it triggered specific checks.

---

Page 23  
```

## Establish a regular access review process for Access Analyzer reports
Customers should establish processes to perform regular reviews of the reports to ensure that only authorized personnel have appropriate access:
- Define a review cadence (e.g., quarterly) for auditing access reports.
- Involve appropriate stakeholders such as IT security, compliance, or application owners.
- Remove or adjust permissions as needed to enforce least access.
- Generate and retain reports regularly to support audit, compliance, and governance activities.

## Implement identity provisioning with SCIM
Review the information on the [System for Cross-Domain Identity Management (SCIM) plugin](#), which enables customers to efficiently provision and manage user identities, group memberships, and additional attributes from external sources using an industry-standard protocol. The SCIM plugin can be used to automate user and group management from sources like Active Directory, AWS, or Okta.

```markdown
### Best practices continued

#### Understand Account recovery (ACR) capabilities
When utilizing Single Sign-On (SSO), ensure that at least one Account Recovery (ACR) administrator is registered prior to activation. This precaution secures fallback access to critical systems should primary authentication methods become misconfigured or unavailable. Thoroughly document all ACR procedures, limit access strictly to authorized personnel, and regularly audit ACR usage to uphold strong security standards. Restrict local logins for interactive sessions to approved recovery users with MFA enabled and employ ACR solely as a recovery tool to maintain system integrity.

ServiceNow colocation facilities are arranged in regional pairs, with all customer production data hosted in both colocation facilities simultaneously. ServiceNow uses asynchronous database replication to keep these pairs in sync.

When performing maintenance, or if an infrastructure component fails, transfer between active and passive colocation facilities is executed as part of ServiceNow standard operating procedures. This ensures that when AHA is needed to address an instance failure, the transfer will be successful and service disruption minimized.

### Determine if your organization requires penetration testing of an instance
As a security best practice, organizations should collaborate with security and compliance teams to identify which ServiceNow instances require penetration testing and establish a clear process for these assessments. This procedure should be reviewed regularly to ensure it remains aligned with evolving security requirements and organizational needs, allowing timely updates if the scope of testing or risk profile changes.

### Define penetration test scope and systematically address findings
For annual application penetration tests, customers are required to install all updates, harden their ServiceNow instance, and meet the prerequisites outlined in the Customer Penetration Testing Policy. After completing these steps, a penetration test can be scheduled.

- Ensure all local account users are enrolled in MFA within the required timeframe ([30 days after first login](#)).
- Monitor local login access to verify MFA enrollment compliance.
- Enforce MFA for admin accounts and roles with elevated access rights.
- Define groups or roles that must always authenticate using MFA, regardless of login method.

## Implement adaptive authentication for granular access control
Collaborate with relevant stakeholders, including security teams, to assess the necessity of implementing Adaptive Authentication policies that limit access exclusively to verified external addresses, such as those originating from the customer’s gateway or web proxy.

```markdown
# File transfers and web services

## Customer responsibility
Customers are responsible to thoroughly review, select and configure the file transfer methods and web services settings used within the instance, ensuring that all security configurations align with their organization’s policies and standards.

---

## Best practices

### Use encryption to secure outbound file transfers during transit
Outbound file transfers from a customer’s instance should use secure protocols such as SFTP, FTPS, or SCP to protect data in transit. Outbound clear text protocols such as FTP and HTTP are also supported but not recommended. Inbound transfers such as web uploads are conducted exclusively over HTTPS.

### Consider limiting file attachment types
Collaborate with stakeholders to determine whether file attachments should be limited by file extension and MIME type. This approach can help prevent potentially malicious files from being uploaded and stored in the instance.

## Use Contextual Security Manager to evaluate table access when possible
The Contextual Security Manager works alongside the broader security framework at ServiceNow, which includes ACLs that can be applied to individual records and fields within tables. This allows for much more sophisticated access control than simple role-based permissions. The plugin is particularly useful when you need security rules that depend on the specific circumstances of the access request rather than just the user’s assigned roles. This makes it valuable for complex enterprise environments where access requirements vary based on data context, business rules, or dynamic conditions.

---

*November 2025 | Release: Zurich*

Page: 21
```

# Penetration testing

## Customer responsibility
Customers may perform application [penetration testing](#) against their sub-production instance(s) in accordance with the ServiceNow Customer Penetration Testing Policy. (Link requires a ServiceNow Support account.)

## ServiceNow responsibility
ServiceNow performs nightly web application security testing using automated and manual techniques, along with third-party security scanning tools.

This process ensures that security assessments are integrated during code development. Findings identified during testing are reviewed by the ServiceNow Product Security Team and forwarded to development for remediation.

Prior to each major release (twice per year), ServiceNow engages an independent third-party to conduct comprehensive application penetration testing using industry-standard methodologies.

## Security_Admin role
[High Security Settings](https://www.servicenow.com) and the [High Security plugin](https://www.servicenow.com) are activated by default on new ServiceNow instances and they can provide an elevated privilege role called `security_admin` role. This role allows users to create and change access controls and change High Security Settings. In the base system, only the default System Administrator (admin) user has the `security_admin` role. The customer admin should work with stakeholders, such as the company’s security team, to determine if an elevated role assignment is required. The `security_admin` role should be assigned to a limited number of users and groups.

---

These policies are regularly updated to address emerging technologies, evolving industry standards, and new security threats.

The ServiceNow AI governance process aligns with the NIST Risk Management Framework for AI and complies with all applicable local laws and regulations. As regulations evolve, we continue to adopt, expand, and align with relevant compliance programs to ensure ongoing adherence.
